# The sortable dashboard's windows start on the first window's theme

## Context

`examples/dashboard/sortable` runs on SharedWorkers. A tile dragged out of the window opens `childapps/widget/index.html?theme=<the tile's theme>` in the same worker. Measured on `dev` at `72f7796f70`, headless Chromium, one browser context:

| Dashboard window | Widget window requests | Widget window opens on |
|---|---|---|
| no request → `neo-theme-neo-light` | `neo-theme-neo-dark` | `neo-theme-neo-light` |
| `?theme=neo-theme-neo-dark` → `neo-theme-neo-dark` | `neo-theme-neo-light` | `neo-theme-neo-dark` |

So a visitor who opens the dashboard, switches it to Neo Dark and drags a tile out gets a light window beside a dark dashboard. Two dashboard tabs with opposite requests show the same: the second tab opens on the first tab's theme.

## The Problem

Both entry points start through `resolveStartTheme(Neo.config)`. In a SharedWorker, `Neo.config` holds the first window's configuration, including its URL, so every later window resolves the first window's `?theme=`, not its own.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/worker/App.mjs` keeps each window's registered configuration in `Neo.windowConfigs[windowId]`, its `url` included (`{base, href, search}` from `src/worker/Manager.mjs`). It sets `Neo.bootingWindowId` around that window's `onStart()`.
- `apps/workstation/app.mjs` and `examples/list/onAir/app.mjs` already resolve from `Neo.windowConfigs?.[Neo.bootingWindowId] || Neo.config`. #21979 moved Dock Choreography to the same lookup after the review found this class there.
- `examples/dashboard/sortable/Viewport.mjs#popupUrl` passes `tile.getTheme()` as the widget window's `?theme=`.

Design authority: #21835, "An example opens on the theme of the catalog that launched it", and the widget entry point's own `@summary`: "Starts a detached tile's window in the theme its dashboard passed as `?theme=`".

## The Fix

`examples/dashboard/sortable/app.mjs` and `examples/dashboard/sortable/childapps/widget/app.mjs` resolve from the booting window's configuration: `resolveStartTheme(Neo.windowConfigs?.[Neo.bootingWindowId] || Neo.config)`. The two-tab spec #21979 added for Dock Choreography covers the sortable windows too, under a name for the class.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With the dashboard open, a widget window opens on the theme its `?theme=` names, in both directions.
- [ ] A second dashboard tab opens on its own request while the first stays open, in both orders.
- [ ] A single window behaves as on `dev`.
- [ ] A browser spec covers the widget window and the two-tab case, red on `dev`.

## Out of Scope

- Changing `resolveStartTheme` itself, or the 35 other examples that call it with `Neo.config`. Their dedicated workers make `Neo.config` the window's own.
- The six toggle examples of #21973.
